text: Time to execute the plan from the kickoff lesson, step by step, on Northbridge Retail's new server, app-02. Every command here is real and runs in the exact order it actually has to.

Creating the deploy user and adding it to the sudo group is step one, but the step that actually matters is confirming it worked — logging in as that user and running sudo whoami, and checking that it genuinely returns root. Everything else in this build depends on that account having real, working sudo access.

Generating an SSH key pair, copying the public half to the server with ssh-copy-id, and then logging in fresh in a new terminal is how you prove key-based access actually works, not just that you configured it. That new session stays open as a safety net for every step that follows.

Setting PermitRootLogin and PasswordAuthentication to no in sshd_config is the actual hardening step, but sshd dash t, which tests the config file for syntax errors before you restart the service, is what keeps a typo from locking everyone out. Only after that check passes does restarting ssh and confirming both settings with sshd dash capital T make sense.

Allowing OpenSSH through ufw before enabling the firewall is the one ordering rule that protects your own connection — enable it first with no exception, and a default-deny policy cuts you off immediately. From there, enabling the systemd service with enable --now and confirming the nightly cron job with crontab -l closes out the hands-on build.

Every piece of app-02's hardening is now in place and verified, one command at a time, in the order that kept you from locking yourself out at any point. Up next, lesson thirty-four: Capstone, Wrap-Up and Portfolio Presentation — checking every piece, then learning how to talk about this project in an interview.
